Navigate the field

Use the arrows, WASD, or swipe the field. The pawn crosses chunk boundaries without resetting the world.

Noise overlays are optional analytical layers. Choose a type to compare spatial structures over the same terrain; seed and coordinates remain deterministic.

Phenomena are independent visual layers: vectors describe direction, particles describe populations, waves describe interference, contours describe scalar structure, topology describes connectivity, and geometry shows coordinate distortion.

Field Guide — what each noise and visual actually shows

How to use this guide: choose a noise overlay or spatial phenomenon above, then open this guide while exploring. Noise overlays colour a sampled field; phenomena draw an additional analytical layer over the terrain. They share the seed and coordinate system, but they answer different questions.

NOISE FUNCTIONS · How the field values are made

Value noise — smooth variation.

Random-looking values are assigned to lattice points and smoothly interpolated between them. In this implementation the interpolation curve is t²(3−2t). Look for broad soft regions rather than isolated random speckles.

Fractal Brownian motion (fBm) — multiple scales.

Several value-noise samples at different coordinate scales are blended together. The displayed overlay weights them approximately 0.55 + 0.30 + 0.15. Large patterns and fine detail coexist, so inspect whether a shape persists as the scale changes.

Turbulence — folded variation.

The implementation takes absolute deviations from the midpoint of noise samples and combines them. Folding positive and negative deviations into magnitude creates sharper, busier transitions. It is a visual transform, not a physical turbulence simulation.

Ridged noise — crests and narrow bands.

A blended noise value is transformed with 1 − |2n − 1|. Values near the middle become high, producing bright ridge-like structures; values near either extreme become low.

Cellular / Voronoi — territories and boundaries.

Seeded feature points are placed in nearby cells, and the distance to the nearest point is measured. This creates cell-like regions. It is useful for studying partitions and neighbourhoods rather than smooth hills.

Domain warp — bend the sampling coordinates.

Two noise samples offset the input coordinates before the terrain noise is evaluated. Increasing the warp control exaggerates bends and folds. Unlike a colour filter, this changes where the field is sampled, so it can reshape other patterns.

SPATIAL PHENOMENA · What the overlays let you inspect

Vector field — local direction.

Short arrows are derived from nearby height samples. The code estimates changes in the x and y directions, rotates that local gradient into a tangent-like direction, and draws an arrow. This helps expose local orientation and variation. It is not a full physical flow model.

Particle field — moving population.

Seeded particles drift with smooth periodic motion and short trails. Their positions are anchored to the global coordinate window and seed, while their movement changes with elapsed time. They are illustrative agents, not particles solving fluid-dynamics equations.

Wave interference — superposition.

Three oscillating sources contribute sine waves based on distance, phase, and time. Their values are summed; the overlay traces places where the combined value is near zero. This illustrates cancellation and reinforcement patterns, not a calibrated physical wave experiment.

Scalar contours — equal-height traces.

The code samples the terrain height repeatedly and highlights near-equal contour levels. Contours make peaks, basins, ridges, and transitions easier to see than surface colour alone. They are a visual sampled approximation, not a precision contour-map export.

Topology — connections between points.

Seeded nodes are connected to their two nearest neighbours. This shifts attention from the terrain's appearance to which points are linked and where clusters form. The result is a nearest-neighbour graph; its edges do not claim physical forces or causal relationships.

Warped geometry — the coordinate grid bends.

A regular lattice is displaced by seeded noise before it is drawn. Compare it with the tile grid to see how a coordinate transformation can distort apparent geometry. This is not, by itself, a physical spacetime model or a metric tensor.

THE MATHEMATICAL PIPELINE

1 · Address: start with a global position (x,y) and a seed. 2 · Transform: optionally perturb the sample coordinates through domain warp. 3 · Evaluate: generate a scalar value such as F(x,y). 4 · Analyse: derive or overlay directions, particles, waves, contours, links, or a warped lattice. 5 · Observe: compare the visual result while keeping track of the parameters.

A compact conceptual notation is F(x,y;s), meaning a field value at position (x,y) under seed s. A warped version can be written Fw(x,y;s) = F(x + wx(x,y), y + wy(x,y); s), where wx and wy are coordinate offsets. These are explanatory notations for the model, not a claim that the simulation represents physical infinity.

Reading results carefully: the seed makes the procedural structure repeatable, but particle motion and wave animation depend on elapsed time. The explorer uses finite-precision JavaScript coordinates and a 2.5D canvas projection. Treat patterns as observations generated by this model; physical or mathematical claims need explicit equations, tests, and defined assumptions.

Trinity of the Unitary Bound Ⅰ · Ⅱ · Ⅲ
One modeled whole, described through three related roles. These are conceptual parts of the model, not claims that physical reality has been proven to work this way.
Ⅰ — ONE SQUARE / DOMAIN

The total field being considered: one domain in which distinctions and positions can be expressed.

Ⅱ — ONE CHUNK / ADDRESS

The fundamental reference unit. Repeating A–G × 1–7 macro addresses and changing micro-localities can create apparent extension without requiring each address to be a separate fundamental container.

Ⅲ — ONE ETERNAL BOUNDARY / LIMIT

The encompassing rule that defines the modeled whole. It need not be a physical wall inside a larger space; it marks the limit of the system as represented.

UNITARY BOUND𝒰 = (D, C, B)D = domain · C = coordinate unit · B = boundary

The three roles are distinguishable but related: the domain gives the address meaning, the address specifies locality, and the boundary defines the whole under consideration. Noise and populators vary the appearance of the field without requiring a new fundamental domain for every variation.

How the infinite illusion works

1. Macro layer: chunk addresses cycle through A–G and 1–7; the layer coordinates track which repetition you occupy.
2. Micro locality: the pawn’s exact global position and the seeded variation rendered around it.
3. Infinite boundary: the conceptual higher-scale system within which macro layers repeat.
4. Apex tier 111: the topmost reference tier above the infinite-boundary layer.
Prototype: 2.5D canvas projection, not a full 3D engine. Infinite coordinates are conceptual; JavaScript uses finite-precision numbers.
